atlas:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: monochrome inventory glyph atlas for a serious post-apocalyptic tabletop game.
Create ONE square 3-by-3 atlas. Nine equal cells in EXACT row-major order, without visible grid, borders or labels. Each active cell contains its ONE requested composition, fully inside that cell, with generous black padding on all sides. Pure solid WHITE silhouettes on perfectly clean BLACK. Flat stencil-like shapes with broad black negative-space cuts; never outline drawings. No gray, colour, gradient, shading, fine engraving, texture, noise, grain, dither or drop shadows. Avoid hairline internal detail: details must remain legible at 16 pixels. Match the restraint, solid coverage and large cutouts of reference image 1. Reference image 1 supplies STYLE ONLY, never its instrument subjects. Reference image 2 supplies the legacy SUBJECTS ONLY: deliberately REMOVE its grid edges, stray pieces, fussy detail and clipping, and use the explicit subject descriptions below instead of tracing its defects. Do not add backgrounds, frames, UI, words, numbers or logos.
CELL 1 (row 1, column 1): ONE complete modern military helmet in side view, with one simple chin strap and one broad ear-protection cut. No floating fragments above it.
CELL 2 (row 1, column 2): A PAIR of complete leg guards, each with a broad knee cup and a long shin plate. Two broad functional sections per guard, clearly legs rather than arms. No feet, straps floating above, rivets or fine seams.
CELL 3 (row 1, column 3): A PAIR of complete compact forearm-and-elbow guards. Broad elbow cap and tapered short forearm shell, without hands. Clearly shorter and wider than the leg guards. No floating pieces.
CELL 4 (row 2, column 1): ONE complete sealed human-proportioned powered police armour suit, standing front-three-quarter view. Helmet with one broad black visor, angular chest shell, two strong shoulder plates, separate hands and feet. Restrained visible powered joints. Slimmer and more human-proportioned than the hydraulic suit in cell 6. No weapons, insignia or ornament.
CELL 5 (row 2, column 2): ONE complete standing suit of improvised SCRAP armour: mismatched broad salvaged sheet-metal plates over torso, arms and legs, a simple rough protective head shell. Uneven silhouette and only a few bold black separation cuts. Clearly improvised plates, NOT a powered robot or medieval knight. No spikes, bolts, tiny lines or weapons.
CELL 6 (row 2, column 3): ONE complete very heavy MILITARY HYDRAULIC armour suit, a stocky industrial colossus with a small closed helmet, huge broad shoulders, thick arm shells and wide feet. One stout simple hydraulic piston visible beside each lower leg. Clearly bulkier than cell 4. Four or five broad black joint gaps, no fine machinery, weapons, gears or spikes.
CELL 7 (row 3, column 1): TWO premium liquor bottles: a broad square decanter with a short stopper and a tall round-shouldered glass bottle with a small cap. Each has at most ONE broad plain black label cutout. Elegant but sober physical objects. No diamonds, words, ornamental facets, border or frame.
CELL 8 (row 3, column 2): ONE cheap squat reused plastic liquor bottle with a simple screw cap, broad shoulders and only TWO broad horizontal rib cuts. A little uneven and utilitarian; no fancy stopper, text or fine texture.
CELL 9 (row 3, column 3): ONE compact rugged medical AUTOINJECTOR beside ONE small capped ampoule, both complete and clearly separated. Thick functional silhouettes and two broad black window cuts. No tick marks, measuring scale, tiny needle, words or medical cross.

Keep the scale and visual weight consistent across cells. Make physical objects immediately recognizable with a handful of bold shapes. No cheerful cartoon styling, decorative fantasy equipment or fine technical illustration.
